title: Observer-Relative Retrocausality in Distributed Information Systems: A Formal Existence Result, Executable Witnesses, and Evidence-Bound Effect Control
abstract_scope: Concise English synthesis of an operational definition, finite theorem, executable witness, physical realization boundary, delayed-choice structural connection, and proposed evidence-bound effect-control profile.

arxiv_metadata_candidate.comments: The paper is a distributed-information-systems manuscript. Its delayed-choice discussion is structural and should not be represented as an independent quant-ph result without a separate physics-focused review.

arxiv-source.tar.gz.role: minimal upload archive containing main.tex and README.md

zenodo_public_record.role: historical QIK-VRT corpus and related materials

ietf_base_document.name: draft-lohmann-qikvrt-effect-ack-03
ietf_base_document.status_boundary: Active individual Internet-Draft; not an RFC, IETF standard, working-group product, consensus result, or IETF endorsement.

claim_boundaries.operational_definition: Observer-relative retrocausality means inverse receiver-local order and authenticated source-reference order for at least one pair of information-bearing records.
claim_boundaries.formal_result: The finite theorem proves the stated relation under its declared order, provenance, information, and monotonicity assumptions.
claim_boundaries.constructive_realization: Positive unequal latencies can realize the operational relation without any signal travelling backwards along its own path.
not_claimed: controllable message into an observer's causal past
independent empirical confirmation of the universe-level correspondence thesis
claim_boundaries.quantum_boundary: Delayed-choice and quantum-eraser experiments are cited as a structural connection for later evidence about earlier records; they do not uniquely select QIK-VRT or establish backward signalling.
claim_boundaries.universe_correspondence: Ingolf Lohmann's explicitly attributed QIK-VRT correspondence thesis, distinct from the finite theorem.
claim_boundaries.ietf_profile: EAP-TPRP is a local, not-yet-submitted companion proposal. It introduces no EFFECT_ACK V1 wire fields and no change to the V1 release predicate.
